title: tessel.toml
description: A Tessel project's file: the version of Tessel it uses, and what the app says about itself. https://tessel-lang.syncster.dev/start/project/

tessel.description: The version of Tessel this project uses, like "0.1.35". Tessel's commands (and editors) hand the project's work to that version, installing it the first time. `tessel pin` writes this.

app.description: What the app says about itself: its bundle on macOS, its .exe's details on Windows, its About panel, and appInfo().

name.description: The app's name, as people see it: the bundle's and the menu's name on macOS, the product name on Windows, the window's title. Default: the app's name in the code.

id.description: A name no other app has, like "com.example.tally". macOS tells apps apart by it: keep it from one version to the next. Default: dev.tessel. and the name.

version.description: The version people see, like "1.2.0". Default: "1.0".

build.description: A build number, for telling builds of one version apart. Default: the version.

description.description: What the app is, in a few words (Windows shows it in the file's Details).

author.description: Who makes the app: a person or a company.

copyright.description: The copyright notice, like "© 2026 Example Surveys".

icon.description: A square PNG, relative to tessel.toml. Default: icon.png next to the code.

category.description: Where the App Store and Finder file the app.

documents.description: The kinds of files the app opens ([[app.documents]]). On macOS, Finder offers the app for them.

name.description: A name for the kind of file, like "Tally Workbook".

extensions.description: The files' extensions, without the dot: ["tly"].

role.description: "editor" (the default) for files the app changes, "viewer" for ones it only shows.
